title: The Sims 3 review (2009)
partialText: Love, work and kleptomania return in The Sims 3, Electronic Arts' enormous life-controlling sequel to the bestselling PC game of all time.

title: This artist 'brings hair to life' by painting video game scenes on the back of wigs, and yes, it really is as impressive as it sounds
partialText: And to think I found haircare to be tedious.

title: No, Richard Dawkins, AI is bloody well not conscious
partialText: And if you think otherwise, you'd better at least attempt to don your philosophy cap.

title: Two Point Museum's latest DLC features a buildable studio where artists can create 'millions' of unique artworks, and there's 'no generative AI involved' whatsoever
partialText: Two Point Museum: Arty Facts is available now.

title: Rust's latest update adds mortars but 'no visual guide to help you land shells,' so get ready for some chaos
partialText: "Firing a mortar requires mastery through trial & error."

title: The next World of Darkness game to be revealed is a Werewolf metroidvania, and I respect the hustle
partialText: They've led by showing gameplay, let's see how that plays out for them.

title: Riven co-creator defends his use of AI art: 'Any artist can take a brush and, without thinking, an artist can create slop'
partialText: The vinyl soundtrack's release should have been a moment to celebrate, instead it's been marked by controversy.

title: Stellaris is 10 years old and still getting DLC, which is impressive
partialText: We talked to some devs about how the space GSG has maintained such a long orbit.

title: Stellaris is getting space nomads and scenarios for its 10th birthday
partialText: Get ready to live out your Battlestar dreams.

title: Pearl Abyss marketing director says Crimson Desert's rapid 'live service' patch cadence is business as usual for an MMO studio: 'That is not normal in the industry. That is normal here'
partialText: "The DNA of the company is inherent in listening to players."

title: Fallout co-creator Tim Cain once proposed a first-person time-travel RPG where you could assassinate historical figures and create paradoxes
partialText: "One, visit 15 different time periods. Two, meet interesting historical figures. Three, kill them."

title: Final Fantasy 14 player harnesses the power of furniture slots to make their in-game house look like Pragmata
partialText: "Increased placement limit is the best!"

title: Double Fine is the latest team at Microsoft to unionize
partialText: The studio behind Psychonauts and Keeper has filed a petition to the National Labor Relations Board.

title: Debate: Is turn-based or real-time-with-pause better for CRPGs?
partialText: Time to relitigate this contentious subject.

title: Discussion time: Are classic tab-target MMOs with loads of keybinds going out of style?
partialText: I can feel my inner old man weeping, but the times, they are a-changing.

title: How a trio of Canadian modders stumbled into making an official Die Hard game: 'I've had projects disappear that had 10 times the promise that this did'
partialText: The strange origin of MechWarrior steward Piranha Games.

title: Can you identify 10 games I've turned into pixelated messes?
partialText: It's time to find out how low res we can go.

title: Gaussian Splatting is my new favourite thing, so I hassled an ex-Epic artist to tell me everything he knows about the low-cost 'photo-real' rendering technique
partialText: "It is not just a rendering trick—it changes the entire capture-to-delivery pipeline."

title: Europa Universalis 5's 'biggest update yet' expands the Balkans, overhauls the economy, and fixes more than 2,000 bugs
partialText: The Encinades update also reworks orthodoxy and improves military systems.

title: Abiotic Factor just got another massive update that adds better pets, a ludicrously involved chemistry system, and most importantly, a mop for cleaning up all your failed experiments
partialText: Cosmic Companions is live now.

title: This very normal Half-Life mod lets you play as 'queen of spacetime' Max Caulfield, and it's convinced me that the next Life is Strange should be a full-on boomer shooter
partialText: Half-Life is Strange adds rewind powers and teen angst into Valve's FPS.

title: Conan Exiles whips out a massive Unreal Engine 5 upgrade that includes an 'enhanced endowment slider' to further improve player penises
partialText: Biggus Clickus.

title: Immediately after putting The Elder Scrolls in Fallout 4, hero modder gets Fallout 1 working on the Pip-Boy too: 'This was so heavily requested, I couldn't pass it up'
partialText: Just get the whole series on there, I guess.

title: Nobody believes Blizzard meant to give Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred players a 900% gold boost, but that hasn't stopped them from exploiting it until someone sticks a decimal point in there
partialText: Get rich with this one easy trick.

title: Morrowind mega-mod Skywind looks so good, even if it's still not finished
partialText: The effort to bring Morrowind into Skyrim continues, and—as always—the team could use some help.

title: Anticipated supercannon sim PVKK delayed until 2027, but for the kind of reason you want to hear
partialText: This just gives us more time to weigh the ethical implications of operating giant weaponry for the baddies.

title: GTA 6's multi-billion-dollar budget is 'a high-stakes game for big boys only,' Take-Two boss says, but he's 'cool with it'
partialText: That's one way of putting it.

title: Sony Interactive Entertainment chief says AI will enable 'gaming experiences like never before,' and I wonder: How long are these guys going to talk about it before we actually start seeing it?
partialText: And do we really want that anyway? I'm not so sure I do.

title: Update: Discord says it's 'seeing significant recovery' after a partial outage
partialText: If you can't start up Discord, it's not just you.

title: Arrowhead addresses the Helldivers 2 community as recent Steam reviews slump to Mostly Negative: 'We want to be clearer about what we're working on and what's coming next'
partialText: Multi-week campaigns, new vehicles, and more red stratagems are all apparently in the works.

title: Microsoft might be all-in on OpenAI now, but back in 2018 thought it was just 'motivated by a need to show how Al can crush humans'
partialText: "We don't want 'machines beating humans' and are not supportive of any push on this."

title: Brigador Killers smacked me in the mouth by making me level a city and kill the protagonists of the first game, and I can't wait for more
partialText: Hardcore.

title: True permadeath: You can never play this game again if you let its immortal snail assassin touch your mouse pointer
partialText: The meme where a killer snail slowly but relentlessly pursues you is coming to your desktop.

title: Elo Shapes reveals a speedy gaming mouse from a fresh new brand that weighs even less than the competition
partialText: Speeding into view.

title: 2K Games confirms layoffs at Project Ethos shooter studio and hints at new design direction: 'It's become clear that changes need to be made'
partialText: The free-to-play extraction/hero shooter was announced in 2024, but hasn't made much headway since.

title: If you're wondering where all the storage is going, it's landed in this 245 TB data center SSD from Micron
partialText: How's your 1 TB HDD feeling now?

title: CCP changed its name rather than pick a fight with the Chinese Communist Party, which was probably wise
partialText: The EVE dev just has fewer armoured divisions, is all.

title: Final Fantasy 14's newest expansion name almost broke the series' 12-year tradition as Yoshi-P 'really wanted' his original idea
partialText: Evercold could have been called something totally different.

title: Rockstar ransom hackers claim to have stolen the data of 280 million teachers, school staff, and students in Canvas attack
partialText: Lock it down, switch on 2FA, and stay safe, folks.

title: Resident Evil Requiem just shadow-dropped a bonus roguelike mode, and it's absolutely fantastic
partialText: Unfortunately, Leon Must Die Forever.

title: Nvidia RTX 5050 review (Palit Dual edition)
partialText: The best budget GPU, though it pains me to say so.

title: Valve forming an orderly queue for the Steam Controller makes it clear we need the same for the Steam Machine, Frame, and perhaps a lot more in-demand tech too
partialText: We need a better system.

title: Chrome is installing a 4 GB local AI model on some of your PCs without asking for permission and will just download it again if you delete it
partialText: 'Chrome did not ask. Chrome does not surface it. If the user deletes it, Chrome re-downloads it.'

title: Videogame 'beta versions' are anything but, says veteran RPG dev—real games are 'sh***y, sh***y, sh***y, sh***y, slightly less sh***y, and it skyrockets' at the end
partialText: Better betas, but better.

title: 'Pearl Abyss created 5,000,000 amateur ornithologists with one update': Crimson Desert's latest patches have effectively transformed it into a birdwatching simulator
partialText: Wait, is that a rare owl?? Sick.

title: Nvidia's VP of deep learning says AI workers are already 'far beyond the costs of the employees'
partialText: How much will AI workers really cost in the end?

title: Sony records a $766 million impairment loss against Bungie for the 2025 financial year, a 1-2 punch of Destiny 2 and Marathon failing to meet its expectations
partialText: Sony bought Bungie for $3.6 billion in 2022.

title: Everything is Crab review
partialText: Survival of the fittest—or at least the most over-levelled.

title: All Genshin Impact 6.6 livestream codes
partialText: Grab the Primogems for the Luna 7 special program.

title: 'Regardless of the type of offer, available capacity is essentially zero right now': SK hynix is reportedly being swamped with 'unprecedented' offers to secure memory chips
partialText: And it seems like it won't slow down for a while.
